verdict.summary: Shopify is self-serve for creating apps, testing, and custom/internal distribution. However, publishing a public app to the Shopify App Store requires passing a formal review by Shopify onboarding specialists.

evidence.note: Shopify allows instant creation of apps and development stores in the Dev Dashboard, but public App Store distribution mandates a review.

verification.note: After you complete the automated checks and prepare your app for submission, you can submit your app for review.

prerequisites.item: A Shopify Partner account with staff permissions 'Build and manage apps' and 'Development stores'

evidence.note: Specific partner staff permissions are required to create apps and development stores.

verification.note: Partner staff members need the Build and manage apps permission to create apps, and the Development stores permission to create dev stores.

steps.title: Choose App Architecture and Distribution Type
steps.detail: Decide between an Embedded App (runs inside Shopify admin via App Bridge), a Standalone/API-only App (runs on external servers using standard OAuth), and whether you need custom distribution (private to a merchant org) or public distribution (App Store listing).
steps.notes: Custom distribution skips the review process but cannot use the Shopify Billing API.

evidence.note: Choosing the right architecture and distribution type dictates review requirements and token flows.

verification.note: Choosing an approach maps each option to its setup guide, covering embedded apps, standalone apps, and custom vs public distribution.

steps.title: Create a Partner Account and App
steps.detail: Log into the Shopify Dev Dashboard and create a new app manually or scaffold it using the Shopify CLI.
steps.notes: Requires human login to the Shopify partner dashboard.

evidence.note: Dashboard registration step.

verification.note: Shopify apps can be built with Shopify CLI or created directly, using the Dev Dashboard.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs and Scopes
steps.detail: Add your exact callback redirect URIs and declare required access scopes in your app settings or config file.
steps.notes: Can be defined in code config files like shopify.app.toml.

evidence.note: Configuring URLs and scopes.

verification.note: You've added your app's redirect URI to your app's settings in the Dev Dashboard, or to the [auth] section of your shopify.app.toml.

steps.title: Obtain API Credentials
steps.detail: Retrieve your Client ID (API key) and Client Secret from the app configuration page.

evidence.note: Credentials required for backend token exchange.

verification.note: You have your app's client ID and client secret from the Dev Dashboard.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth Flow
steps.detail: Redirect merchants to the authorize endpoint, validate the state nonce, verify the HMAC signature, and exchange the code via POST request.
steps.notes: Standard server-side implementation using client_id and client_secret.

evidence.note: OAuth flow details.

verification.note: In this tutorial, you'll learn how to do the following tasks: Redirect a merchant to Shopify's authorization page, Validate the callback, Exchange the authorization code...

steps.title: Test via Custom Distribution / Development Store
steps.detail: Install your app on a development store to test OAuth installation and API calls without public review.
steps.notes: Development stores allow free testing of custom and standalone app flows.

evidence.note: Custom distribution bypasses store review.

verification.note: Mentions custom distribution and dev dashboard/admin apps, but does not explicitly detail testing via a development store in this specific forum post snippet.

steps.title: Submit for App Store Review (Optional)
steps.detail: If building a public app, prepare compliance webhooks, fill out submission forms, and submit the app for review.

evidence.note: Public distribution review process.

verification.note: Start your app review journey on the Shopify App Store review page. You'll be guided to complete mandatory fields and automated tests...
